description: GitLab access tokens — three flavours. Personal Access Tokens (`PAT`) follow the user; Project / Group Access Tokens are scoped to one project or group; Deploy Tokens are credential pairs for read-only registry / repo pulls in CI. Self-hosted GitLab uses the same shapes.

variants.description: User-scoped `glpat-…` token. Inherits the user's permissions across every project they can access. Right for local development / CLI use; avoid in CI where a Project Access Token tracks the project boundary cleanly.
variants.format_hint: starts with `glpat-`, 20 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-] after the prefix

steps: Open https://gitlab.com/-/user_settings/personal_access_tokens (self-hosted: replace gitlab.com with your host)
Pick a name describing where the token will live (`devboy-laptop`, `ci-pipeline`)
Set an expiration — required since GitLab 15.4, max 1 year
Pick scopes (`api` for full read/write; `read_api` if read-only)
Click Create personal access token, copy the value (shown once)
retrieval.notes: Self-hosted GitLab on a private host is fine — but make sure the host is publicly reachable from devboy if you want liveness probes to succeed. The `api` scope grants every action your account can perform; lean on `read_api` whenever the tool only reads.

variants.description: Project-scoped `glpat-…` token issued under a service-account identity. Stays valid even when the human who created it leaves; right for CI bots and project-bound automation.
variants.format_hint: starts with `glpat-`, 20 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-] after the prefix (same shape as a PAT)

steps: Open the project's Settings → Access Tokens page
Pick a name describing the bot (`ci-deploy-bot`, `release-publisher`)
Set an expiration — required, max 1 year
Pick a role (`Maintainer` for CI; `Developer` is enough for read+pipeline-trigger)
Pick scopes (`api`, `read_repository`, `write_repository` are the common ones)
Click Create project access token, copy the value (shown once)
retrieval.notes: Project tokens automatically create a service-account user that counts against the seat limit on paid GitLab plans. Group Access Tokens (one level up) are similar in shape — same regex, same liveness — and cover every project under the group.

variants.description: Username + token pair scoped to a project. Read-only against the registry, repo, or package registry — the workhorse for `docker login` and `git clone` in CI without burning a Project Access Token seat.
variants.format_hint: no prefix, opaque alnum string of provider-defined length

steps: Open the project's Settings → Repository → Deploy tokens
Pick scopes (`read_registry` for `docker login`, `read_repository` for `git clone`)
Click Create deploy token, save BOTH the username and the token value (each shown once)
retrieval.notes: Deploy tokens authenticate as `gitlab-deploy-token-<id>` rather than as a user. There is no liveness URL that pairs with a Deploy Token alone — verify by attempting the operation it was issued for (e.g. `docker login` against the project registry).
